Rashi on Yevamot 6a:10:1.hebrew: והא תנא בעלמא גמר - לאוי דטומאה והעלם אבדה מלאוי דשבת, ולא פריך:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:10:1.english: But didn't the tanna derive in general - [He derives] the prohibitions of ritual impurity and ignoring a lost item from the prohibitions of Shabbat, and he does not object.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:11:1.hebrew: תיפוק לי מהתם - מאיש אמו ואביו תיראו, דהכשר מצוה הוא ולא דחי. למה ליה למיהדר למכתב הכא את שבתותי תשמורו? אלא לאו דתילף מיניה, דאפילו בלא הכשר מצוה, אי לא כתיב קרא בהדיא דלא דחי — אמרינן דדחי? אם כן, איצטריך עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:11:1.english: Let it be derived from there - From [the verse]: “You shall fear every man his mother and his father” (Leviticus 19:3), for it is [merely] preparation for a mitzva, and it does not override [Shabbat]. Why did [the Torah] need to return and write here, “You shall keep My Shabbatot” (Leviticus 19:30)? Rather, is it not [in order] to derive from it that even without [it being merely] preparation for a mitzva, if Scripture had not explicitly written that it does not override, we would say that it overrides? If so, [the word] aleha [“upon her” (Leviticus 18:18)] was necessary [to prohibit a forbidden relative from levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:12:1.english: Keeping is stated with regard to Shabbat, and reverence with regard to the Sanctuary - And Scripture juxtaposed them in a single verse.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:1:1.hebrew: לאו דמחמר - אחר בהמה, שהוא בלאו דלא תעשה כל מלאכה אתה ובהמתך (שמות כ׳:י׳). ובהאי לאו ליכא כרת, דלא עביד מעשה בגופיה, וכמ"ד בפ' מי שהחשיך (שבת דף קנד.): המחמר אחר בהמתו בשבת — פטור:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:1:1.english: The prohibition against driving [an animal] - [Driving] behind an animal, which is included in the negative prohibition: "You shall not do any work... you and your animal" (Exodus 20:10). And with this negative prohibition there is no karet [spiritual excision], for he does not perform an action with his [own] body; and [this is] in accordance with the one who said in the chapter [entitled] "Mi Shehechshikh" (Shabbat 154a): "One who drives [a laden] animal on Shabbat is exempt."

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:1:2.english: And even so, [it does] not override - [This is said] in astonishment, as a question.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:2:1.english: And let us derive from here - That it does not override even a mere negative commandment.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:3:1.hebrew: וכי תימא שאני לאוי דשבת דחמירי - דקי"ל (עירובין דף סט:) מחלל שבת כעובד עבודת כוכבים, ומשום הכי אפי' לאו גרידא לא דחי, ומנייהו לא גמרינן:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:3:1.english: And if you say that the prohibitions of Shabbat are different because they are severe - For we hold (Eruvin 69b) that one who desecrates Shabbat is like one who worships idols, and because of this, [a positive commandment] does not override even a mere negative commandment, and we do not derive [other prohibitions] from them.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:3:2.hebrew: והא תנא בעלמא קאי ולא פריך - והא אשכחן תנא בעלמא דיליף שאר לאוי — כגון לאו דלא יטמא דכהן ולאו דלא תוכל להתעלם — מלאו דשבת לחומרא, ולא פרכינן: שאני לאוי דשבת דחמירי:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:3:2.english: And behold, the tanna speaks generally and does not object - Behold, we find a tanna in general who derives other negative commandments — such as the negative commandment of “he shall not defile himself” regarding a priest and the negative commandment of “you may not hide yourself” — from the negative commandment of Shabbat to be stringent, and we do not object: The prohibitions of Shabbat are different, as they are [more] severe.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:4:1.english: His father said to him - To a priest.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:4:2.hebrew: היטמא - בבית הקברות להשיב אבידה, או שהיתה עומדת בחוץ ואמר לו: אל תחזיר — יכול ישמע לו? ת"ל: איש אמו ואביו. וילפינן לאו דטומאה ולאו דהשבת אבדה מלאוי דשבת:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:4:2.english: Be rendered ritually impure - [That is, to enter] a cemetery to return a lost item; or where [the lost item] was standing outside, and he said to him: “Do not return [it]” — might [one think] he should obey him? The verse states: “A man, his mother and his father [you shall fear, and My Sabbaths you shall keep]” (Leviticus 19:3). And we derive the negative commandment of [ritual] impurity and the negative commandment of returning a lost item from the negative commandments of Shabbat.

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:5:1.hebrew: אלא - לעולם דאמר ליה: שחוט לי, בשל לי, ואפ"ה לא איצטריך עליה, דאיכא למיפרך: מה להנך שחוט לי, בשל לי — שכן הכשר מצוה בחילול שבת, בעקירת לא תעשה הוא מקיים עשה דכיבוד, וזהו הכשר קיומו, ואי אפשר לקיימו בלא עקירת לאו. הלכך, אי לא כתב את שבתותי תשמורו, ה"א לידחי. אבל ייבום — לא זה בלבד הכשר קיום העשה, שהרי יכול לחלוץ ולא יעקור לאו של ערוה, ולא איצטריך עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:5:1.english: Rather - In truth, [the baraita speaks of a case] where he said to him: 'Slaughter for me,' 'Cook for me,' and even so, ['beside her'] was not needed [to prohibit levirate marriage with an incestuous relation], for there is [this] refutation: What [is unique] about those [cases of] 'Slaughter for me,' 'Cook for me'? That the preparation for the mitzva is through desecration of Shabbat; by uprooting a negative commandment he fulfills the positive commandment of honoring [his father], and this is the preparation for its fulfillment, and it is impossible to fulfill it without uprooting the negative commandment. Therefore, had [the verse] not written 'You shall keep My Shabbatot,' I would have said that it should override [it]. But [regarding] levirate marriage, this is not the only preparation for fulfilling the positive commandment, for he can perform chalitza and not uproot the negative commandment of an incestuous relation, and ['beside her'] would not be needed [on that account].

Rashi on Yevamot 6a:8:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בבונה וסותר - איצטריך למיסר, אף על גב דאב מלאכה הוא ואיכא כרת. אי לאו דאשמועינן, ה"א: אתי עשה דועשו לי מקדש ודחי לאו דשבת:
Rashi on Yevamot 6a:8:1.english: What, is it not [referring to] building and demolishing - It was necessary [for Scripture] to forbid [them], even though it is a primary category of labor and entails karet. For had it not taught us [this], I would have said: Let the positive commandment of "And they shall make Me a sanctuary" come and override the negative commandment of Shabbat.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:12:1.hebrew: יכול יתיירא אדם מבית המקדש - גבי אביו לא הוצרך לומר כן, דפשיטא שלא ישתחוה לו לשם אלהות; אבל גבי המקדש איצטריך, משום דהוי דבר שבקדושה. א"נ: גבי אביו שייך מורא, שלא יכעיסנו; אבל במקדש אין יכול למצוא אלא בדוחק, כמו שמפרש והולך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:12:1.english: "One might think that a person should revere the Temple" - With regard to one's father, it was not necessary to state this, for it is obvious that one would not bow down to him as a deity; but with regard to the Sanctuary it was necessary, because it is a sacred entity. Alternatively: with regard to one's father, reverence is applicable [in the sense] that one should not anger him; but with regard to the Sanctuary, one can find [how reverence applies] only with difficulty, as [the baraita] goes on to explain.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:2:1.hebrew: ניגמר מהכא דלא דחי - משמע: דאי איירי בשחיטה ובישול, ניחא. ותימה: דמנא ליה לתנא לאוקמי קרא בשחיטה ובישול לאשמועינן דבעלמא דחי? אדרבה, נוקמה בלאו דמחמר, ונגמר מהכא דבעלמא לא דחי אפילו לאו גרידא! וי"ל: דדייק תנא מדלא אשמועי' קרא בשאר דברים דליכא אלא לאו גרידא, דלא הוה אתי למיטעי. וא"ת: והיכי נגמר מהכא דלא דחי? דלמא שאני הכא דהוי עשה ולא תעשה — דהא כתיב (למען ינוח שורך וחמורך וביום השביעי תשבות) (שמות כג) — ומש"ה הוא דלא דחי, אבל לאו גרידא לעולם נילף מכלאים בציצית דדחי! ואר"י: דעשה דכיבוד, הואיל ועדיף כולי האי דהוקש כבודם לכבוד המקום, חשיב עשה דשבת כמאן דליתיה לגמרי, והוי כמאן דליכא אלא לאו גרידא. וכמו כן עשה דמקדש ועשה דבת כהן עדיפי מעשה דשבת, משום מורא ומשום כפרה דבת כהן. וא"ת: מנלן דלא דחי עשה דכיבוד אפי' לאו גרידא? דהא שבת, וטומאה, והשבת אבדה — כולהו עשה ולא תעשה נינהו! וי"ל: כיון דגלי לן קרא דלא אלימא לן טעמא דהוקש כבודם לכבוד המקום דלידחי — א"כ אפילו לאו גרידא לא דחי, דמכלאים לא מצי גמיר, משום דכיבוד הוי הכשר מצוה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:2:1.english: "Let us derive from here that it does not override" - This implies that if [the verse] were dealing with slaughtering and cooking, it would be well. And it is puzzling: For from where did the Tanna know to establish the verse as [referring to] slaughtering and cooking, [in order] to teach us that elsewhere [a positive commandment] overrides [a negative commandment]? On the contrary, let us establish it as [referring to] the prohibition against driving [a laden animal] (meḥammer), and let us derive from here that elsewhere [a positive commandment] does not override even a mere negative commandment! And it can be answered that the Tanna inferred [this] from the fact that the verse did not teach us regarding other matters where there is only a mere negative commandment, [since] one would not have come to err [regarding them]. And if you say: But how could we derive from here that [a positive commandment] does not override [a negative commandment]? Perhaps here is different, as it is a positive and a negative commandment — for behold, it is written: ("that your ox and your donkey may rest, and on the seventh day you shall rest") (Exodus 23) — and it is because of that that it does not override; but as for a mere negative commandment, we should always derive from diverse kinds [kilayim] in ritual fringes [tzitzit] that it does override! And the Ri said: Since the positive commandment of honoring [one's parents] is so superior, in that their honor was equated to the honor of the Omnipresent, the positive commandment of Shabbat is considered as though it does not exist at all, and it is as though there were only a mere negative commandment. And likewise, the positive commandment of the Sanctuary and the positive commandment of [executing] a priest’s daughter are superior to the positive commandment of Shabbat, because of reverence [in the case of the Sanctuary] and because of atonement in the case of a priest’s daughter. And if you say: From where do we know that the positive commandment of honoring [parents] does not override even a mere negative commandment? For behold, Shabbat, [priestly] impurity, and returning a lost item are all a positive and a negative commandment! And it can be answered: Since the verse revealed to us that the reason "their honor was equated to the honor of the Omnipresent" is not powerful enough for us that it should override — if so, it does not override even a mere negative commandment, for it cannot be derived from [the case of] kilayim, because honoring [parents] is [only] preparation for a mitzva.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:3:1.hebrew: והא תנא בעלמא קאי ולא קפריך - קשה, דמשמע דאי איירי בשחיטה ובישול ניחא ליה. ואדרבה, כ"ש דקשה טפי: דהיכי יליף דהיטמא ולא תחזיר דליכא כרת, משבת דאיכא כרת וסקילה? דנהי דהתם לא דחי — הכא דחי, אע"ג דאיכא לאו ועשה, משום דהוקש כבודם! ויש לומר: כיון דגלי קרא דגרע מעשה דעלמא — דבעלמא דחי לאו שיש בו כרת, והאי לא דחי — תו לא מהני טעמא דהוקש כבודם לכבוד המקום:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:3:1.english: "And the tanna speaks generally and does not raise a difficulty" - This is difficult, for it implies that if [the baraita] were dealing with slaughtering and cooking [on Shabbat], it would be fine [to derive that a positive commandment does not override a prohibition]. And on the contrary, all the more so it is even more difficult: for how could he derive [the prohibitions of] "be rendered impure" and "do not return [a lost item]," where there is no karet, from Shabbat, where there is karet and stoning? For granted that there [on Shabbat] it does not override, here [in regular prohibitions] it should override — even though there is a negative commandment and a positive commandment — because their honor was equated [to the honor of the Omnipresent]! And one can say: Since the verse revealed that it is inferior to a general positive commandment — for generally [it was presumed that] a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment that carries karet, whereas this [positive commandment of honoring parents] does not override — the rationale that "their honor was equated to the honor of the Omnipresent" is no longer effective.

Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:6:1.hebrew: שכן הכשר מצוה - פירוש בקונטרס: לעולם בשחוט לי, בשל לי, והא בעלמא דחי; מ"מ לא נילף מהכא דלידחי עשה דייבום לאו דאחות אשה, משום דאיכא למיפרך: שכן הכשר מצוה, דאי אפשר לקיים הכיבוד בלא דחיית הלאו, אבל גבי ייבום יכול לקיים המצוה בלא דחיית הלאו, דאפשר בחליצה. וקשה לר"י: דאין זה אפשר, דאי אסור לייבם משום כרת — חליצה נמי לא בעי, דכל שאין עולה לייבום אין עולה לחליצה, ולקמן בפ"ב (יבמות דף כ. ושם) ילפי' מקרא. ועוד אמרי' בההיא שמעתא (דף כא.), דלא חשבינן גבי יבום אפשר לקיים שניהם ע"י חליצה, משום דחליצה במקום ייבום לאו מצוה היא. (ועוד, דלקמן לפי האמת דאיכא קרא בכלאים, ל"ל קרא, כיון דהכשר מצוה דוחה אפי' ל"ת שיש בו כרת?) ועוד, דמסקינן דבשום מקום אין עשה דוחה ל"ת שיש בו כרת — משמע אפילו בהכשר מצוה. ולקמן דפריך: "הכשר מצוה תיפוק לי מהתם", דפי' הקונט': תיפוק לי מהתם, מכיבוד אב דלא דחי, אלא ודאי ההוא דמקדש אתא למימר הא בעלמא דחי אפי' בלא הכשר מצוה — ואין זה דיוק; דדלמא לגופיה איצטריך: משום דמכיבוד ילפינן דבעלמא דחי, איצטריך למיכתב גבי מקדש דלא דחי. ומיהו הא איכא למימר: אף על גב דבעלמא דחי, גבי מקדש ה"א דלא דחי כמו בכיבוד, דבכל מילי דשבת ה"א דלא דחי, ולהכי איצטריך מילה ופסח ותמיד, וכן אומר מהרר"י. ונראה לר"י, וכן פירש רבינו חננאל, דבלאו דמחמר מוקי לה; ומהכא לא נילף בעלמא דלא לידחי לאו גרידא, דמה לכיבוד שכן הכשר מצוה: כשמחמר, ומטמא, ומניח מלהחזיר אבדה כדי להביא גוזלות לאביו — בשעת דחיית הלאו אין מאכילו ומלבישו, אבל בעלמא דעביד גוף המצוה ילפינן מכלאים בציצית דדחי. ואר"י: דכיבוד אב אפי' עוסק בגוף מצוה לא דחי, דבכל ענין קא פסיק שלא ישמע לו; והיינו משום דברוב ענייני כיבוד רגילים להיות על ידי הכשר מצוה, קאמר רחמנא דלא דחי בכל ענין. והשתא לקמן פריך שפיר: הכשר מצוה תיפוק לי מהתם דלא דחי, ואם אינו ענין להכשר מצוה תניהו ענין לגוף מצוה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 6a:6:1.english: "As it is preparation for a mitzva" - The explanation in the Kuntres [Rashi] is: Actually, [the baraita speaks of a case where the father says:] "Slaughter for me," "Cook for me" [acts carrying the penalty of karet], and behold, elsewhere [a positive mitzva] overrides [even a prohibition of karet]; nevertheless, we would not derive from here that the positive mitzva of yibbum should override the negative commandment of a wife’s sister, because it can be refuted: for it is the preparation for the mitzva [i.e., the only way to fulfill it], since it is impossible to fulfill the honoring without overriding the negative commandment, whereas in the case of yibbum, one can fulfill the mitzva without overriding the negative commandment, as it is possible [to fulfill it] through ḥalitza. And the Ri finds this difficult: For this is not [a valid case of] "it is possible [to fulfill through ḥalitza]"; for if it is forbidden to perform yibbum on account of [the penalty of] karet, she does not require ḥalitza either, as [the rule is that] anyone who is not eligible for yibbum is not eligible for ḥalitza, and later in the second chapter (Yevamot 20a and there) we derive [this] from Scripture. Furthermore, we say in that sugya (21a) that regarding yibbum, we do not consider it [an instance where] it is possible to fulfill both [the positive commandment and the negative commandment] by means of ḥalitza, because ḥalitza in place of yibbum is not a mitzva. (And furthermore, later, according to the ultimate truth that there is a verse regarding kil’ayim [in tzitzit, from which we derive that a positive mitzva overrides a negative commandment], why do I need a verse [such as "aleha" to teach that yibbum does not override an ervah], since preparation for a mitzva [according to this reasoning] overrides even a negative commandment that carries karet?) And furthermore, we conclude [in the Gemara] that nowhere does a positive commandment override a negative commandment that carries karet — which implies even in [a case of] preparation for a mitzva. And as for that which [the Gemara] challenges later (6a:11): "Let preparation for a mitzva be derived from there," regarding which the Kuntres explains: "Let it be derived from there, from honoring a father, that it does not override; rather, certainly that [verse] regarding the Temple came to say: behold, elsewhere it overrides even without preparation for a mitzva" — this deduction is not [necessarily] exact; for perhaps [the verse regarding the Temple] was needed for its own sake: since from honoring [parents] we [would have] derived that elsewhere it overrides, it was necessary to write regarding the Temple that it does not override. However, this [much] can be said [in support of the Kuntres]: Even though elsewhere [a positive commandment] overrides, regarding the Temple I would have said that it does not override, just as with honoring [parents], for regarding all matters of Shabbat I would have said that it does not override; and for that [reason] circumcision, the Paschal offering, and the daily offering were needed [to teach that they override Shabbat]. And so says Maharri. And it appears to the Ri, and so explained Rabbeinu Chananel, that [the Gemara] establishes [the baraita] in the case of the negative commandment of driving an animal [meḥammer]; and from here [honoring parents] we do not derive regarding elsewhere that [a positive commandment] does not override an ordinary negative commandment. For what [can be deduced from] honoring [parents]? For it is merely preparation for a mitzva: when one drives an animal, or becomes ritually impure, or refrains from returning a lost item in order to bring fledglings to his father — at the time he overrides the negative commandment, he is not [yet] feeding him or clothing him! But elsewhere, where one performs the essence of the mitzva itself, we derive from kil’ayim in tzitzit that it does override. And the Ri said: Honoring a father does not override [a prohibition] even when one is engaged in the essence of the mitzva, for [the baraita] ruled categorically that he should not obey him in any circumstance; and that is because since most matters of honoring [parents] are normally [performed] by means of preparation for a mitzva, the Merciful One stated that it does not override in any circumstance. And now, later [the Gemara] properly challenges: "Let preparation for a mitzva [not overriding Shabbat] be derived from there [from honoring parents], that it does not override!" And if [the verse by the Temple] is not relevant to preparation for a mitzva, apply it as relevant to the essence of the mitzva.
